title: Quantification of ruffle area and dynamics in live or fixed lung adenocarcinoma cells
protocol: Run the FIJI/ImageJ plugin: Plugins › Registration › Correct 3D drift for drift/jitter correction.
Crop out the black bars around the stack by drawing a rectangular ROI and running Image › Crop.
Crop the time series before bleach correction to eliminate debris or cells moving in and out of the field of view.
Save processed images as separate TIFF files from original data.
Measure ruffle area over time using FIJI/ImageJ software.
Open FIJI/ImageJ.
Drag an image set into FIJI such as the preprocessed data from the previous section.
Identify a cell forming or disassembling a ruffle within the duration of the time-series in FIJI.
Set up measurements in FIJI: Analyze › Set Measurements...
Select “Area” and “Display label”.
Use an appropriate number of decimal places for measurements.
Go to Analyze › Set Scale... to check if the pixel to distance conversion scale was imported.
Enter the conversion if not already imported.
Select the Freehand selections tool in FIJI.
For each frame of the ruffle, draw an ROI around the ruffle.
Press Ctrl + M or M to run the Measure plugin (also Analyze › Measure).
Copy data from the Results table into a spreadsheet.
Process collected ruffle area data to analyze dynamics of ruffle formation.
Calculate lifetime of ruffles by counting total number of frames they are present and converting to time.
Determine maximum area of each ruffle from the measurements made previously.
Calculate time of appearance for each ruffle using the first row of the "Label" column in the ruffle area data.
Calculate the closing rate starting from the final value and working backward.
Define a minimum number of frames for opening and closing phases as 4 frames each.
Set a minimum R2 value of 0.7 for accuracy in calculations.
Define the stability phase between the last frame of the opening phase and the first frame of the closing phase.
Enter measurement values in a spreadsheet using clean data principles.
Save the processed data file in CSV format.
After collecting images of actin and nuclei staining, analyze the images to quantify the average ruffle area per cell.
Set up measurements in FIJI by selecting “Area” and “Display label” under Analyze › Set Measurements...
Go to Analyze › Set Scale... to check if the pixel to distance conversion scale was imported. If not, enter the conversion manually.
Run Image › Adjust › Threshold... (or Ctrl + Shift + T).
Select “Dark background,” then adjust the top slider to set the threshold for only the ruffles and make note of the threshold values.
Set threshold values manually for subsequent images.
Optional: Apply median filter before thresholding to reduce noise while preserving edges.
Run Analyze › Analyze Particles...
Set size range of particles; use default setting if appropriate.
Select “Summarize” and leave other options unselected.
Click “OK”.
If analyzing a multichannel image, select “No” when prompted to process all images.
Copy the “Total Area” value from Summary window into spreadsheet along with number of cells.
Note units of total area value: microns² if scale conversion was set previously; otherwise in pixels.
Sum all total area values and cell numbers for each condition in spreadsheet software.
Divide summed ruffle area by summed number of cells to calculate average ruffle area/cell for each condition.
